    WinPirate14=<clr><clrEnd>    Upon parking your trusty ship for good, you began the organizational efforts for the good of the pirate clan. Though you never did become a pirate baron, your experience as a ranger proved invaluable in pulling off various ambitious projects, starting from one pirate planet and ending with the entire star sector. <br> <br>    Fourteen years after you've exchanged a pilot's cockpit for a paper-laden office table, you were nominated for the post of planetary ruler. You scored a resounding victory on election day, garnering overwhelming support. Upon making it to the top, you remained there until your retirement, eventually surrendering your chair to a young and promising up-and-comer. After stepping down, you proceeded to spend many a long winter night telling your grandkids about your adventures fighting the dominators, as well as hundreds of other fascinating stories from your rich ranger past.
    WinPirate15=<clr><clrEnd>    Your contribution to victory against the dominators was substantial. As a result, you became the public's darling. For several years following the war, your face was a staple on stereovision and in newspapers, and a few books were even written about your ranger career. You constantly received invitations to become a showman or a politician. It didn't take you long to realize that it was essentially the same profession, only with different titles. You fielded every offer of this type with a polite yet firm refusal. <br> <br>    Once peace was firmly established in your arm of the Galaxy, the ranger core was disbanded with honors. A grand ceremony was organized for the occasion, at which all of the war's participants were awarded. You were nabbed to host the event, which ended up being a wonderful time. You were especially glad to see your former companions with whom you had braved many a battle. <br> <br>    Most of the former rangers returned to civilian life. As for the others, who were particularly restless, you proposed to resume your collaboration by founding a new elite security agency. In only a few short years your firm and its quality of service became the stuff of legend throughout the Galaxy, bringing you more business than you could hope to handle. No pirates or extremists could match the skill of your brave companions and former Coalition fighters. Though financial security arrived at almost the very beginning of your new career, you kept working as the company head to a ripe old age, ultimately retiring an extraordinarily respected person.
    WinPirate16=<clr><clrEnd>    If not for your support, it's doubtful that the pirates could have beaten the dominators on their own. Indeed, it was their great fortune that a skilled fighter such as yourself was on their side. Alas, not all bandits supported your opposition, with many opting to hide in the rear, but those that followed you proved enough to bring the entire Galaxy back into pirate hands.<br> <br>    Once the dominator threat was destroyed, you suddenly found yourself without a job. With no more enemies left to fight and all of your associates from the pirate clan settled in political posts, the younger pirate generation quickly forgot who it was that had saved them from swarms of ruthless robots. After spending a few eventful years in bars, getting sloshed and telling war tales, you realized the futility of your behavior and decided to retire from the grind of modern life. After choosing an unpopulated planet with a habitable though not entirely hospitable climate, you built yourself a home in the bosom of nature, growing food in your own private garden and fishing from a nearby lake. <br> <br>    Many years into your new reclusive life you spied a spaceship in the sky. Nursing a vague but unrelenting anxiety, you decided to hide in the nearby woods just in case. The visitors were a bunch of goons who burned your hut to the ground for the hell of it, broke all the equipment and trampled the entire garden. Unable to endure their defiling the fruits of your labor, you grabbed a heavy stick and ran over to the house. Thanks to your athletic shape and unforgotten ranger skills, you proceeded to give the punks a good thrashing and were within an inch of winning... But then a shot rang out. One of the bandits was armed. <br> <br>    They threw your body into the fire and ran off. <br> <br>    It wasn't until several decades later that the Galaxy learned of your fate, having discovered your ship hidden in the woods. Your favorite meadow has since become a popular pilgrimage site, with a monument to your heroic deeds erected right in the middle.
    WinPirate17=<clr><clrEnd>    If not for your support, it's doubtful that the pirates could have beaten the dominators on their own. Part of the blame lay squarely on your shoulders, as it was you who, before defeating the dominators, had terminated the pirate leader who had been pushing for the integration of the pirate clan with the highest rungs of the Coalition hierarchy. In so doing you brought back the era of pirate outlaws, with each pirate answering to no higher authority and acting without any regard for others. Provisional pirate governments, established in the course of opposing the dominators, rushed to secure their grip on power the moment the robot enemy was no more, while various pirate capos and khans vied against them, anxious to take their turn at the helm of whole planets. <br> <br>    The upshot of all this bedlam was that in a few short years the various planetary governments quarreled with one another over race, politics, morality, religion and every other issue imaginable, leading to an all-out war. Relations between maloqs and pelengs became especially volatile, and nothing could keep the two races from getting at each other's throats. The virtually unheard of religious cult known as Game Developers of Dawn strode into public eye by capturing an entire star system, then migrating everybody, people and planets and all, to a different arm of the Galaxy. <br> <br>    In the early stages of the chaos you tried your best to talk sense into all the parties and calm the situation. Upon realizing the futility of your efforts, you gave up and settled on one of the primitive agrarian planets undisturbed by war and uprisings, not even news of the madness that had overtaken the Galaxy. It was there that you lived out the rest of your days, leaving this world a decrepit bag of bones. Many centuries later, when peace finally returned to the Galaxy, the historians honored you with a dubious title -- the lamest hero in the history of the Galaxy.
    WinPirate18=<clr><clrEnd>    Upon defeating the dominators, you garnered your share of glory. However, putting your face on screens all over the Galaxy led to your ship being attacked by a well-organized group of pirate assassins mere days later. Realizing that the pirates would never leave be the one who had exposed their wicked plans and beheaded their organization, you knew that you had but one choice -- to disappear. The Coalition special forces staged an accident in which your ship collided with a large asteroid, followed by a grand funeral for the hero of the Coalition, the broadcast of which you watched on stereovision.<br> <br>    With new documents and a new identity, as well as a healthy bank account, destiny was yours to decide. You could have spent the rest of your days on the Galaxy's finest interstellar resorts. Or you could have accepted the job offer from the Coalition's Intelligence Agency and become instructor for a new generation of special agents. You could have even started on a memoir in the style of a sci-fi novel or learned to play an ancient human instrument called the accordion...<br> <br>    But, as it happens, one day you found yourself standing outside a military training facility, your eyes fixed on a poster: "The Galaxy Needs Space Rangers!" It felt as though your decision was made for you then and there...

Thanks to you, the word of a noble pirate once again rang loud and true across the Galaxy!<br> <br> Despite your contentious reputation, you managed to live a long and happy life, commanding great respect among not only your brothers-in-arms, but also their enemies. Tales of your courage and sense of justice became the stuff of legend, passing from generation to generation via not only the latest technologies, but just as they would in the good old times: from a human to a maloq, from a maloq to a peleng, and from a peleng -- for a reasonable fee, to be sure -- to the rest of the world.
    WinPirate7=<clr><clrEnd>    Realizing that the pirates would not rest until the person responsible for exposing their wicked schemes and beheading their organization was punished, you decided to simply disappear. The military may take pride in their fancy uniforms, but in the Klissan War three hundred years ago, as they suffered one defeat after another, it was the rangers who solved the mystery of Makhpella and put an end to the most terrible war in the history of this sector of the Galaxy! The rangers are no cannon fodder, capable only of obeying orders; every ranger is his own general and supply battalion!

They are called the dominators and represent a new form of cyberlife. As of yet, we do not know why they have begun attacking us, both on our planets and in space. Most dominator robots have only a semblance of intelligence, so it stands to reason they are controlled by brain centers. Initially it was believed that they had only one such center, but this presumption proved a costly mistake for the Coalition fleet at the Battle of Gralgar! Now we know that there is a minimum of three such centers, each controlling its own series of dominators. We were able to learn the origin of these robots and some things about their inner workings, but this information is classified. Perhaps you will be granted access to it at a later date. Besides, now is not the time for lectures -- the dominators have already captured tons of planets, and our fleet is still struggling to recover from the Gralgar massacre!
    Text=<br>But that's not all! Taking advantage of the fact that brave warriors are occupied with the robot invaders, pirates have crawled out of the woodwork as well, bending weakened Coalition systems to their will! The pirate threat was shrugged off at first, but it has become painfully clear that they pose as much risk to our civilization as the dominators! Now we find ourselves waging a two-front war, and the Coalition forces remain the weakest link in this struggle. This means that space rangers have once again become our last hope for survival. And now the only thing keeping you from eternal glory is a medical examination. But between you and me, due to the desperate situation on both fronts, the doctors were given a secret directive to give all candidates a clean bill of health! Dismissed, soldier!

FormRuinsSB ^{
    Continue=Next
    History ^{
        PlayerOk=Tell me about the Klissan War
        SB=Today we can offer you a free presentation on the history of the Klissan War. An aspiring ranger ought to know their history.
        SBOk=Gaals were the first to encounter the klissan -- this happened many centuries before their contact with the other Coalition races. Back then the gaalian civilization didn't consider territorial greed as a sign of barbarity, or introspection and moderation as wisdom, pursuing a policy of active galactic expansion. Having settled numerous worlds in adjacent sectors, the gaals wanted to reach the next spiral arm of the Galaxy. This was considered unfeasible, as entering and exiting the hyperspace is only possible in places where the continuum is distorted by the gravitational pull of particularly massive objects, such as stars.  Moreover, "penetrating" the continuum between the two zones consumes energy, more of it as the distance increases. In contrast, spiral arms are separated by countless parsecs of emptiness; to penetrate them in one trip you'd need a truly colossal supply of energy, perhaps that of an entire star. Sure, you could also follow the spiral: the local arm to the center of the Galaxy, then back along the next, but that kind of journey is too long even for gaals to undertake. So the gaals chose a third option, made possible by the new technology of stable "bubbles" of distorted space, capable of teleportation independent of the mass that generates them. Such a "bubble" has made it possible to travel virtually anywhere in the known cosmos.
        SBOk1=The gaals promptly used it to reach the neighboring arm and found the first colonies in the system of a star they went on to call Elthane. From there their expansion proceeded smoothly, until one of the fleets tasked with exploring the second arm had a chance encounter with Makhpella. Makhpella was a giant sentient ship -- a product of abiological evolution. She was moving from one star to another with an entourage of her own -- a fleet of smaller subordinate "ships," called the klissan. That first encounter ended in tragedy, with the klissan destroying the entire gaalian expedition. And so began the war, in which the gaals suffered one defeat after another. And it wasn't just their fleet detachments that were perishing: Makhpella and the klissan would wipe out every living creature on every colonized planet they could reach...
        SBOk1=The gaals that had stayed behind in our spiral arm were spared this awful fate, but the shock of it all had steered the course of their civilization in a completely new direction. Further expansion in space has become far less popular than before. The bubble-generating technologies were outlawed and classified to all but the highest echelons of government. The damages to science and other intellectual pursuits were equally great, as many scholars and scientists had rushed into the new arm, eager to explore the new frontier, and were now dead.
        SBOk2=In the centuries that followed the gaalian civilization began to gradually recover, getting back to space exploration, establishing contact with the fae, the pelengs, the maloqs and the humans, and assisting in the formation of the Galactic Council. And then, three hundred years ago, when it seemed as though a time for lasting peace has come, Rachehan came and ruined everything. Formerly one of the top commanders in the peleng fleet, he became incensed when he was passed over for a promotion and decided to turn to piracy. Before making his move official, he went to work for the national intelligence agency, where he came across an old gaalian archive that had been long forgotten by everybody else. Upon learning about the secret of "bubbles" and Makhpella, he theorized (correctly, as it turned out!) that there were many such Makhpellas out there. Of course, he had little need of Makhpella initially. The bubble technology was more than sufficient to pirate all over the known space with impunity, emerging anywhere at will and disappearing back into hyperspace.
        SBOk2=Desperate, the five civilizations formed a common anti-terrorist strike force which managed to lure the pirate fleet into a trap. It was a massacre, but Rachehan still managed to escape with his life. It was then that he decided to fly to the adjacent spiral arm and seek out Makhpella, aiming to either gain control over the superweapon or set it on the united governments' forces. As you might expect, plan A didn't quite work out for him. Plan B, however, worked out beautifully, as Makhpella and the klissan chased him right into our spiral arm.
        SBOk3=As the second war waged on, it was hardly more successful than the first. Though five civilizations were putting up a better fight against the klissan than the gaals alone, they were still losing, however gradually. And so the five races gambled on the rangers, hoping that small autonomous vessels would succeed where massive fleets had failed -- get close to Makhpella and destroy her. Funny how the military always strives to destroy the enemy, rather than try and understand their motives... Fortunately, there were those in the scientific community who aspired for the latter. Little did they know that they had a champion among the rangers, shrewd enough to use the latest technologies to establish direct contact with Makhpella. Amazingly, it turned out that Makhpella never meant anybody harm! The Makhpella race is inorganic in nature, having emerged from the gas-and-dust nebulae in space; their bodies constitute a myriad tiny crystalline elements, combining in different forms when placed in an energy field. And the klissan (contrary to the initial theory that they were her subjects or offspring) turned out to be remotely controlled organs which Makhpella could cultivate in great numbers. Makhpellas travel through space, feeding on the energy of stars and showing very little interest in planets. This interest was further diminished after a visit to a random planet proved catastrophic -- the native bacteria entered the organism and proceeded to destroy Makhpella crystals as it spread. Consequently, when the first and the second Makhpella encountered our civilizations, they mistook the lifeless spaceships for sentient beings, and the crews manning them for organic parasites!  Makhpellas never even considered the possibility that organic life could be intelligent. As such, their cause was a noble one: to stop the organic plague from spreading...
        SBOk4=Once the misunderstanding was clarified, Makhpellas were no longer a threat. They live in their own arm of the Galaxy, while we live in ours. Wicked tongues have dubbed that war the War of Delusion... And rightfully so, seeing as our governments try their damnedest to avoid any mention of it...
        SBOk4=But now you also know everything there is to know about that war, <Player>. Perhaps this knowledge will prove useful to you in the future.
    }
}

Tips ^{
    00=This is a hint. An ordinary hint can be deleted by a right-click.<br>    Some important hints cannot be deleted until you complete or fail the related quest.<br>    To save a game, go to Menu (<clr>ESC<clrEnd>) and press Save (<clr>F2<clrEnd>). To load a previously saved game, press (<clr>F3<clrEnd>).
    01=To take off from a planet, enter a Hangar (<clr>H<clrEnd>) and command takeoff (<clr>F<clrEnd>).
    02=Hangars are used to repair the hull of your ship, refuel and take off from a planet. For your convenience, a robot in the upper part of the screen will always inform the pilot about breakdowns of the ship's vital systems (hull, engine, fuel tank) or absence thereof. Here the player can also check the other ships currently docked in the same spaceport.
    03=Learn to control the camera by moving the cursor to one edge of the screen, then the other. You can also move the camera by holding down the left mouse button and moving the cursor on the radar, or by holding down the right mouse button on any open area of space. Mouse over a ship, planet or any other significant object to display a hint with the description and characteristics of the object.<br>    To find your ship again, press on the Search button on the radar (<clr>C<clrEnd>).
    04=To land on a planet or a station, double-click on it. The ship will then head to the planet and land.
    05=To speak with the government, click on the Government menu button or press (<clr>G<clrEnd>) on your keyboard.
    06=To go to the trade center, click on the Trade Center menu button or press (<clr>T<clrEnd>) on your keyboard.
    07=The trade center window is divided into two parts. On the left is the list of available goods and their prices on this particular planet. On the right are the goods in your cargo bay and the prices at which you can sell them. Some of the goods might have a thumbs up symbol next to them. When on the left side, it means that the purchase price is good (i.e. cheap); when on the right side (which displays the contents of your cargo bay), it means that selling the merchandise is to your advantage (sale price is higher than purchase price).<br>    Clicking an item in the left side of the window will bring up the Purchase window. Clicking an item in the right side of the window will open the Sell window.
    08=To approach an asteroid, double-click next to it. The ship will then fly to the chosen spot.
    09=To destroy an asteroid, go to the weapons menu or press (<clr>W<clrEnd>) on your keyboard. Having chosen a weapon, select a target and press End Turn. If the weapon's range is too small, close in on the object.<br>    To fire from all weapons without going to the weapons menu, press (<clr>~<clrEnd>) on your keyboard.
    10=To pick up minerals/cargo, you must be in the immediate proximity of them. When you mouse over a mineral the cursor will change to a hand and a pickup radius will be drawn around the ship. Click on all the minerals you want to pick up, making the selected minerals with the hand icon. Then press End Turn (<clr>SPACEBAR<clrEnd>), and the ship will pick up the minerals within the pickup radius. To collect the remaining minerals you must move closer to them.
    10=If you double-click on a specific mineral, the ship will automatically move closer and pick it up.
    10=Make sure you have sufficient space in your cargo bay. If an object is big and doesn't fit in the available space, you will not be able to pick it up. Also, you will not be able to pick up an object without a gripper or if the gripper is not powerful enough.
    11=To find out if your ship is equipped with a gripper and its capacity, open the Ship window (<clr>S<clrEnd>).
    11=This window displays all of your property. Mouse over an item to see its properties. You can also manipulate items. Pick up the engine and move it into the cargo bay. Close the Ship window (<clr>Esc<clrEnd>), and you will discover that you cannot fly. To fix the problem, reopen the Ship window and return the engine to its original position.
    12=To make a hyperjump, open the Galaxy Map (<clr>M<clrEnd>). Then click the star you want to jump to within your hyperengine's operating radius (displayed as a circle with your current location in the center). A path to this star system will be charted on the map. Press Hyperjump. The Galaxy Map window will close and the ship will lay a course to the target star system. Press End Turn (<clr>SPACEBAR<clrEnd>). The ship will fly to the edge of the current system and make a hyperjump.
    13=To refuel, enter the Hangar (Hangar button or <clr>H<clrEnd>), and press Refuel (<clr>B<clrEnd>). The button will only be available if your fuel tanks aren't filled to the brim.
    14=To engage another ship in battle, open the weapons menu (<clr>W<clrEnd>). Upon choosing a weapon, select a target and press End Turn. Press (<clr>~<clrEnd>) to select all available weapons.
    15=To pursue a ship, left-click on it once. Click on the ship again to select one of three possible combat options:
    15=- <clr>Standard pursuit<clrEnd>. Suitable for pursuing civilian targets. In this mode your ship will follow the target at the closest possible distance.
    15=- <clr>Combat pursuit<clrEnd>. Recommended for difficult fights. In this mode your ship will try to keep the target just within your firing range.
    15=- <clr>Autocombat<clrEnd>. In this mode your ship will maneuver and use weapons automatically. Recommended for easy fights.
    15=You can select the default pursuit mode in Settings.
    15=When double-clicking on an object, you will automatically end your turn and your ship will fly over to the target.
    16=If there is another ship within your radar range, you can communicate with it. To do that, press Talk (<clr>T<clrEnd>) and click on the ship you want to talk to.<br>    While in talk mode, you can demand money and cargo from other captains, urge them to attack other ships, or give orders to your partners.<br>    If your ship is equipped with a scanner, you can try to scan other ships. To do that, press Scan (<clr>I<clrEnd>) and click on the object. If your scanner is powerful enough, you will see the target ship from the inside.
    17=All rangers can have other ships under their command -- so-called partners. In order for a partner to help you in a battle you must inform them of your plans. Your partner will always appear on the radar as an icon. Left-click on the icon quickly find your partner, right-click on the icon to open a dialogue window and give orders to them. Before starting a dialogue with your partner, click on the target you want to direct them to. For instance, if you are landing on a planet, you can order your partner to land on it too. The same applies to pursuing ships and hyperjumps.
    18=A black hole is actually a hyperspatial gate to other systems. Inside the hole there are hyperspatial clusters of matter, where you can encounter hostile ships from other galaxies. If that happens, only by destroying all the enemies can you exit the cluster.
    18=Controls inside of the cluster are manual: Forward, Back, Left, Right. Fire by pressing <clr>CTRL<clrEnd>. Be ready, for you will need great courage and lightning-fast reflexes to defeat a cunning enemy. If things get rough, hand the controls over to the autopilot.
    18=During a hyperspace fight you can collect various bonuses that may either increase or decrease your chances at victory. Simply fly over a bonus to pick it up.
    18=To pick up an object in hyperspace, get close and click on it. The object will not be picked up if it's outside gripper range, if the gripper isn't powerful enough or if there's not enough space in your cargo bay.
    18=Your enemies' artifacts and equipment will be your reward for victory in the black hole. Due to its non-standard construction, equipment picked up in black holes cannot be upgraded using micromodules. However, it can strengthen the effect of certain artifacts.
    18=Be careful: when flying into a black hole you lose the ability to change equipment and weapons until you find an exit.
